title: Lists
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Lists in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: What is a list?
items.text: A list is an ordered, changeable collection. Lists are written with square brackets.

items.heading: List indexing
items.text: List items use zero-based indexing, so items[0] is the first item.

items.heading: List mutability
items.text: Lists are mutable, which means their contents can be changed after creation.

items.heading: append()
items.text: append() adds one item to the end of a list.

items.heading: pop()
items.text: pop() removes and returns an item, and without an index it removes the last item.

items.heading: remove()
items.text: remove(value) deletes the first matching value from a list.

items.heading: len()
items.text: len(list) returns the number of items in the list.

items.heading: sort()
items.text: sort() changes a list by sorting it in place.

items.heading: sorted()
items.text: sorted(items) creates and returns a new sorted list without changing the original list.

items.heading: Mixed values
items.text: A Python list can contain values of different types, although a consistent type is often easier to work with.

items.heading: List slicing
items.text: A slice can select a range of list items without changing the original list.
